title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change

key_patterns.name: Multiplex social structure
key_patterns.description: Agents have distinct family, work/school, and community layers with different sizes and expected contact strengths.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence strengths and contact rates should be modeled; family ties typically yield stronger behavioral influence.

key_patterns.name: Degree heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Per-layer degree sequences are likely right-skewed; some agents have many community/work ties (potential super-spreaders of information/behavior).
key_patterns.relevance: Heterogeneity accelerates diffusion; calibration should preserve tail behavior (use overdispersed distributions).

key_patterns.name: Homophily by age_group and occupation
key_patterns.description: Edges likely assortative by age_group (e.g., students with students) and occupation; family layer strongly age-structured.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily affects local prevalence and cluster-level adoption; include mixing matrices when generating networks.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception aligns with adoption
key_patterns.description: Higher risk_perception correlates with higher initial_mask_wearing and higher ongoing adoption propensity.
key_patterns.relevance: Map risk_perception to lower thresholds or higher adoption probabilities.

key_patterns.name: Information drives adoption and persistence
key_patterns.description: In the panel, receiving information on day t increases probability of wearing_mask on day t; persistence from t-1 to t is high; dropout exists but is rarer.
key_patterns.relevance: Calibrate separate adoption and retention probabilities conditional on info exposure.

key_patterns.name: Adjacency reciprocity/symmetry issues
key_patterns.description: JSON adjacency lists may be directed; reciprocity is not guaranteed and duplicates across layers may exist.
key_patterns.relevance: Decide whether to enforce undirected edges per layer; reconcile duplicates and validate degree constraints.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(a, b) by MLE: a,b > 0

key_distributions.name: Initial mask seed rate
key_distributions.description: Share of agents with initial_mask_wearing = true.

key_distributions.name: Per-layer degree distributions
key_distributions.description: family, work_school, community degrees per agent; total_connections is their sum.
key_distributions.parameters: Negative Binomial(mu_l, k_l) per layer l ∈ {family, work_school, community}; also record max degree and Gini for tails

key_distributions.name: Age and occupation composition
key_distributions.description: Categorical distributions of age_group and occupation.

key_distributions.name: Information exposure frequency
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of received_info in the panel; heterogeneity across agents likely.
key_distributions.parameters: Population: Bernoulli(r_info). With heterogeneity: Beta-Binomial with Beta(α_info, β_info) prior across agents

key_distributions.name: Behavioral transitions
key_distributions.description: Discrete-time transition probabilities of wearing_mask given prior state and info.
key_distributions.parameters: p_adopt_info = P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t-1}=0, info_t=1); p_adopt_noinfo; p_stay_info = P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t-1}=1, info_t=1); p_stay_noinfo

key_distributions.name: Layer overlap
key_distributions.description: Probability that a dyad appears in multiple layers (e.g., family also co-workers in family businesses).
key_distributions.parameters: Overlap rate ρ_overlap = |E_family ∩ E_work| / |E_union| etc., and Jaccard indices per layer pair

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association; higher risk perception correlates with initial adoption.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression or rank correlation; expect moderate

key_relationships.relationship: Higher degree agents receive info more frequently via neighbors.
key_relationships.strength: Positive; magnitude depends on per-edge info transmission probability

key_relationships.relationship: Students/White Collar/Blue Collar differ in work/school degree distributions.
key_relationships.strength: Strong; capture via occupation-layer mixing and degree priors

key_relationships.relationship: Family degree varies with age group (e.g., middle-aged higher).
key_relationships.strength: Moderate to strong; use as constraints during degree assignment
To be calibrated; expect larger effect for family layer

age_group_distribution.value: Empirical category probabilities from agents CSV (normalize counts of age_group)
age_group_distribution.notes: Use to sample new populations or to weight mixing matrices

occupation_distribution.value: Empirical category probabilities from agents CSV
occupation_distribution.notes: Align with work/school degree targets per occupation

risk_perception_distribution.notes: If multimodal, consider mixture of Betas or empirical resampling

initial_mask_seed_rate_p0.notes: Initialize mask state at t0 by agent; p0 used when bootstrapping

adoption_threshold_mapping.value: theta_i = max(0, min(1, theta0 - alpha * risk_perception_i))
adoption_threshold_mapping.notes: Alternative: probabilistic adoption via logistic model with risk_perception coefficient

num_agents.value: N = number of rows in Agents CSV (or keys in JSON adjacency)

degree_distributions_per_layer.notes: Estimate mu, k by MLE; cap extremes to ensure graphicality

mixing_matrices.source: Network JSON (observed edges) or generated via heuristic if not present
mixing_matrices.notes: If JSON missing or directed, infer by symmetrized edges

edge_symmetry_rule.value: Undirected edges per layer; symmetrize JSON by taking union of adjacencies
edge_symmetry_rule.notes: Keeps degree targets close to CSV; log discrepancies

layer_overlap_rate.value: ρ_overlap per layer pair computed from JSON
layer_overlap_rate.notes: Use to allow multilinks or to weight co-layer edges

per_edge_transmission_prob.source: Calibrate to match received_info rate in train_data.csv given degree distributions
per_edge_transmission_prob.notes: Estimate via moment-matching: E[info_t] ≈ 1 - Π_neighbors(1 - beta_l * mask_neighbor_t-1)

exogenous_broadcast_rate.source: train_data.csv residual info events not explained by network
exogenous_broadcast_rate.notes: Fit after setting beta_l; equals observed info rate minus network-predicted rate

information_memory_length.source: Schema implies info at day t affects adoption same day
information_memory_length.notes: Extend to multi-day memory if panel suggests lag effects

layer_influence_weights.source: Behavioral theory and to be tuned against train_data transitions
layer_influence_weights.notes: Initialize with priors; calibrate via simulated method of moments to match adoption speed

adoption_model.value: logit P(wear_t=1) = β0 + β1*wear_{t-1} + β2*info_t + β3*f_weighted_masked_neighbors_{t-1} + β4*risk_perception + β5*(risk_perception × f_neighbors)
adoption_model.notes: If only train_data available, fit β0..β2; set β3..β5 via calibration with simulated network exposures

adoption_probability_for_non_wearers.notes: Use as baseline; can be modulated by neighbor fraction and risk

update_order.value: 1) Generate info via network and exogenous; 2) Update wearing_mask given info and neighbors

targeting_rules.value: Optional: prioritize high-degree or central agents for seeding interventions

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage semi-likelihood calibration. Stage 1 (network): If Network JSON is authoritative, use it directly and measure layer-specific degree distributions, clustering, overlap, and mixing matrices for validation. If only degree targets exist, generate networks per layer via a configuration model constrained by empirical degree distributions and mixing matrices; allow multilinks if ρ_overlap > 0. Stage 2 (behavior): From train_data.csv, estimate transition probabilities p_adopt_info, p_adopt_noinfo, p_stay_info, p_stay_noinfo and a baseline logistic model with predictors wear_{t-1} and received_info. Next, calibrate social influence weights (w_family, w_work_school, w_community) and per-edge info transmission rates (beta_l) using simulated method of moments: choose parameters that match (a) average daily received_info rate, (b) time series of mask prevalence and incidence, and (c) stratified adoption curves by degree and risk_perception quantiles. Optionally refine via Bayesian calibration (ABC or particle filtering) if likelihood is intractable.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out the last T_val days per agent for temporal validation. Validate: (1) Prevalence trajectory: RMSE/MAE between simulated and observed mask prevalence over time. (2) Transition matrix: compare observed vs simulated p_adopt_info/noinfo and p_stay_info/noinfo. (3) Info exposure rate: match marginal P(received_info) and its heterogeneity across agents (Beta-Binomial fit). (4) Stratified fits: prevalence by age_group, occupation, and degree deciles. (5) Network features: degree distributions, clustering coefficients, and mixing matrices per layer (if network is generated). (6) Sensitivity analysis: vary key parameters (w_l, beta_l, θ parameters) and report elasticity of outcomes. (7) Posterior predictive checks if Bayesian: reproduce joint distribution of (wear_t, wear_{t-1}, info_t).
key_variables_to_calibrate: β0, β1, β2, β3..β5 in adoption logistic
theta0 and alpha (risk-to-threshold mapping) or equivalent
homophily mixing matrices per layer (if generating network)
layer overlap rate ρ_overlap (if generating network)

file_summaries:
- Data structure and type:
  - CSV file where each row represents a single agent (node) in the simulation.
  - Columns include numeric (age, risk_perception, connection counts), categorical (age_group, occupation), boolean (initial_mask_wearing), and an integer ID.

- Meaning of keys/columns:
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for each agent (primary key).
  - age: Agent’s age (numeric).
  - age_group: Categorical age band (derived from age; useful for group-specific rules).
  - occupation: Categorical role (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar) that can proxy daily contact contexts.
  - risk_perception: Continuous [0,1] measure of perceived risk; higher values imply greater propensity to adopt mask-wearing.
  - initial_mask_wearing: Boolean seed state for mask adoption at t0.
  - family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections: Intended degree (number of ties) per social layer.
  - total_connections: Sum of the three layer-specific degrees (redundant check: equals their sum in samples).

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No nested structures; flat schema.
  - Implicit relationship: total_connections = family + work_school + community.
  - Layer-specific connection counts imply a multiplex network (three layers: family, work/school, community) per agent.

- How this data should inform simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: Instantiate one agent per row with attributes (age, age_group, occupation, risk_perception, initial_mask_wearing).
  - Network generation: Build a three-layer network where each agent’s degree in each layer matches the corresponding connection count; total_connections can validate construction.
  - Dynamics:
    - Initialization: Set mask state from initial_mask_wearing.
    - Influence: Use layer-specific edges to propagate behavior; optionally weight influence by layer (e.g., family > work/school > community) and/or by occupation/age_group.
    - Heterogeneity: Map risk_perception to adoption thresholds or probabilities (e.g., higher risk_perception lowers threshold or raises adoption probability given masked neighbors).
  - Calibration/validation: Check degree realizability per layer and that sums match total_connections; use age_group/occupation to parameterize contact frequency or homophily during edge assignment if desired.

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object mapping agent IDs (as strings) to per-agent records.
  - Each record contains arrays of integer IDs representing neighbors in different social layers.
- Meaning of keys or columns:
  - family: close-kin ties; typically small, strong, high-frequency contacts.
  - work_school: coworkers/classmates; medium-sized network with structured, repeated contacts.
  - community: broader, weaker ties (neighbors, acquaintances, social activities).
  - all: deduplicated union of family, work_school, and community neighbors for that agent.
- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Top-level keys (e.g., "0", "1", "2") are unique agents; values are layer-specific adjacency lists.
  - Neighbor IDs are integers referencing other agents in the same global index space.
  - The graph is multi-layer: the same pair of agents can be connected in multiple layers.
  - Reciprocity is not guaranteed by the file itself; treat edges as undirected only if reciprocity is enforced/validated, otherwise as directed adjacency lists.
- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agents: one agent per top-level key; number of agents = number of top-level keys.
  - Network structure: build a multiplex network (separate graphs per layer or a single graph with layer-tagged/weighted edges).
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Use layer-specific contact frequencies/weights (e.g., family > work_school > community) when computing social influence on mask adoption.
    - Time-of-day or context-based scheduling can activate layers differentially (home vs work/school vs community periods).
    - The all list enables quick neighbor aggregation when layer context is not needed; prefer layer lists when modeling heterogeneous influence strengths.
  - Initialization: the file provides topology only—no attributes like initial mask status, susceptibility to influence, or thresholds; these must be assigned externally (e.g., random, degree-based, or homophily-based).
  - Analytics: degree, centrality, clustering can be computed per layer and used to target seeding or interventions.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

- Overall structure and type:
  - CSV file in long (panel) format.
  - Each row is a daily observation for a specific agent.
  - Primary key: (agent_id, day). Time is discrete and synchronous across agents (unit: day).

- Columns and meanings:
  - day: Integer time index (timestep).
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an agent, consistent across days.
  - wearing_mask: Boolean state indicating whether the agent is wearing a mask on that day (interpretable as end-of-day state).
  - received_info: Boolean flag indicating whether the agent received mask-related information on that day (an event/exposure during the day).

- Relationships and temporal dependencies:
  - Temporal sequence per agent: wearing_mask at day t is expected to depend on wearing_mask at day t-1 and received_info at day t (and possibly prior info history).
  - No network/edges are present; received_info is recorded as an outcome, not explained by social ties here. In the simulation, received_info should be generated by the social network diffusion and/or exogenous broadcasts to match this variable’s role.

- How this informs simulation entities and interactions:
  - Agents:
    - State variables: wearing_mask(t), info_received(t).
    - Optional latent traits to fit: adoption propensity/threshold, persistence/forgetting.
  - Dynamics:
    - Use the data to estimate discrete-time transition probabilities or a logistic model:
      - P(wear_t = 1 | wear_{t-1} = 0, info_t)
      - P(wear_t = 1 | wear_{t-1} = 0, no info_t)
      - P(wear_t = 1 | wear_{t-1} = 1, info_t)
      - P(wear_t = 1 | wear_{t-1} = 1, no info_t)
    - These govern adoption, retention, and dropout in the simulation after info events occur.
  - Information process:
    - In the simulation, received_info should be produced via social network contagion (neighbor-to-neighbor transmission) and/or exogenous campaigns so that its marginal rate aligns with the empirical frequency in the data.
  - Initialization and validation:
    - Initialize agents’ wearing_mask at day 0 from the data (if provided) and calibrate transition parameters from observed transitions.
    - Validate by reproducing trajectory of mask-wearing prevalence and transition rates.

- Practical notes:
  - Ensure rows are sorted by (agent_id, day); handle any missing days (impute or treat as no observation).
  - CSV booleans may be strings (“true”/“false”); cast explicitly.
  - The update order implied by the schema: information arrives during day t, then wearing_mask state is realized for day t. Define this same order in the simulator.
